Interface VirtualView

All Known Implementing Classes:
VirtualViewTCP
public interface VirtualView
Server-side contract for a virtual view that receives client commands.

A virtual view is the boundary object that represents one connected client inside the server. It hides the concrete transport from the server logic: TCP, RMI, or any other protocol can receive a client command in a different way, but the server only needs a structured ClientMessage, a way to record pong replies, and a way to close the session.

This interface describes the inbound side of a virtual view, from client to server. The outbound side, from server to client, is represented separately by Listener, which receives server payloads and sends them through the concrete transport.

  • Method Details

    • handleClientMessage

      void handleClientMessage(ClientMessage clientMessage)
      Passes a structured client message from the transport layer to the server.

      Implementations normally attach their session id and delegate the payload to the routing layer, so the command reaches the correct pre-lobby, lobby, or game controller.

      Parameters:
      clientMessage - client command already parsed from the transport protocol

    • pong

      void pong(PongPayload payload)
      Handles a pong response received from the client.

      The pong belongs to the connection keep-alive protocol, not to game logic. Implementations use it to refresh the session activity timestamp through the server connection lifecycle.

      Parameters:
      payload - pong payload received from the client message envelope

    • closeSession

      void closeSession()
      Requests closure of the client session represented by this virtual view.

      The interface does not prescribe how the concrete transport is closed. Implementations are responsible for performing their own cleanup and for triggering the server-side disconnection flow.
